en.title: Rome II: which event must a choice of law follow under Article 14(1)(a) when several events give rise to the damage?
en.summary: Article 14(1)(a) allows a choice by an agreement entered into after the event giving rise to the damage. Where several events give rise to the damage, for example a first act in one country and a final act in another, and the parties are not all pursuing a commercial activity, the text does not say which event the agreement must follow.
en.impact: An agreement made between the earliest and the last event can be valid under one reading and invalid under the other.
en.correction: The Commission's work on the application of the Regulation could say which event counts.
